pr.body:
- move sidebar above top layer UI (especially top-right) so that buttons aren't above the sidebar when open
- close sidebar (when not docked) when opening main menu. This is necessary otherwise the previous change would make the main menu below the sidebar on mobile.
pr.title: fix: close floating sidebar on main menu open

plain.fix: The sidebar now draws above all top-bar buttons. To avoid the new overlap on phones, opening the main menu now also closes a floating sidebar. The mechanism that stopped the menu from accidentally closing itself when you clicked its own button was also updated to match the new structure.
plain.title: Sidebar draws above all buttons, and closes when the main menu opens
plain.problem: When the sidebar was open, some toolbar buttons in the top-right corner appeared on top of it, covering it. Fixing that by raising the sidebar higher would cause a new problem on phones: the main menu would open underneath the sidebar.

steps.headline: Sidebar and main menu overlap in the wrong order
steps.narration: The sidebar is a panel that slides in from the right side of the canvas. There are two related problems. On desktop, toolbar buttons in the top-right corner draw on top of the open sidebar, covering it. The fix for that — raising the sidebar's stacking order — creates a second problem on phones: the main menu drops down from the top-left button and, if the sidebar is already open, the sidebar would now sit above the menu and cover it.

steps.say: The sidebar used a z-index of 80, but top-right buttons ran at 100 — so they always drew on top.

lines.annotation: Top-right UI buttons draw here — above the sidebar.

beats.text: At base, `--zIndex-ui-library` is 80; `--zIndex-ui-top` is 100. The sidebar uses the former, the top bar the latter.
beats.heading: Z-index values at base

beats.text: The sidebar's `z-index: var(--zIndex-ui-library)` (80) loses to `z-index: var(--zIndex-ui-top)` (100) on any positioned top-bar element.

traces.label: buttons render on top of sidebar

beats.heading: What breaks

steps.title: Sidebar z-index was below the top bar
steps.headline: Sidebar's stacking order was below top-bar buttons
steps.narration: The sidebar and the top-bar buttons both use named z-index variables. The sidebar used the library variable, which was set to 80. The top-bar buttons used the top variable, set to 100. Because 100 wins over 80 in the stacking order, any button in that top-bar layer appeared above the open sidebar, covering it.

steps.say: Moving the variable below the modal threshold but above the top-bar puts the sidebar in the right order.

lines.annotation: Now above ui-top (100); sidebar draws over top-right buttons.

beats.text: `--zIndex-ui-library` is raised from 80 to 120 and repositioned in the list to be above `--zIndex-ui-top`.
beats.heading: What we change

steps.title: Raise the sidebar above the top-bar layer
steps.headline: Sidebar z-index raised above top-bar buttons
steps.narration: The fix for the stacking problem is simply to give the library variable a higher number. The new value of 120 sits above the top-bar at 100, below the context menu at 90 — wait, actually above both context menu and top bar, but below modals at 1000. The variable is moved in the source list to reflect its new position in the stacking hierarchy.

steps.say: With the sidebar at 120, it now outranks the main menu on mobile. Both can be open at once, so the sidebar must close when the menu opens.

steps.headline: Higher sidebar now covers the main menu on phones
steps.narration: On mobile, the main menu drops down from the hamburger button in the top-left corner. Before this fix, the sidebar sat behind the top-bar layer and also behind the menu. Now that the sidebar is higher, it sits above the main menu. If both are open at the same time the sidebar covers the menu, so the next step must close the sidebar whenever the menu opens.

steps.say: The sidebar already closes when you click outside it. If clicking the menu trigger counts as an outside click, the sidebar closes automatically — no new code needed in the menu.

This stops ALL useOutsideClick handlers — including the sidebar's — when the button is clicked.

steps.title: Close sidebar via the sidebar's own outside-click handler

sources.ref: sidebar closes on outside click; removing the guard lets that path handle the menu trigger

steps.headline: Let the sidebar's existing close path do the work
steps.narration: The sidebar already has an outside-click listener that closes it when you click anywhere outside the panel. If clicking the main menu trigger button counts as an outside click, the sidebar closes without any new code in the menu itself. The only thing blocking that was the guard on the trigger button that told every outside-click listener to ignore it. Removing that guard lets the existing sidebar close path handle the job.

steps.say: Removing the attribute would make the menu close itself when you click its trigger. The fix wraps trigger and content in a shared container and checks that instead.

lines.text: // remove this div from box layout

lines.annotation: Both trigger and open content are now children of this element.

beats.text: `DropdownMenu` now renders a `<div class="dropdown-menu-container">` around both the trigger and the open content. `display: contents` removes it from box layout so it does not affect visual rendering.
beats.heading: Step 1 — wrap trigger and content in a container

lines.text: // prevents closing if clicking on the trigger button

lines.annotation: If the click is inside the wrapper (i.e., on the trigger button), skip — menu will not close itself.

beats.text: The menu content's `useOutsideClick` callback walks up to the nearest `.dropdown-menu-container` and skips if the clicked element is inside it. This is the new substitute for the `data-prevent-outside-click` attribute.
beats.heading: Step 2 — check container in the outside-click handler

lines.annotation: Removal lets the sidebar's outside-click handler see taps on the menu trigger.

beats.text: With the container check in place, `data-prevent-outside-click` is removed from the trigger button. Clicking the trigger is now visible to the sidebar's outside-click handler, which closes the floating sidebar.
beats.heading: Step 3 — remove the attribute from the trigger

steps.title: Replace the attribute guard with a DOM-container check
steps.headline: Menu no longer guards itself with a global attribute
steps.narration: A guard on the trigger button previously told every outside-click listener in the app to ignore clicks on it. Removing that guard naively would mean clicking the trigger fires the outside-click callback on the menu itself, immediately closing it. Instead, the trigger and content are wrapped in a shared container, and the menu's own outside-click handler checks whether the click landed inside that container before deciding to close. This keeps the toggle behaviour intact while letting the sidebar's listener see the click and close the sidebar.

steps.say: A supporting type change so the new container check can read which element was clicked.

lines.text: /** if performance is of concern, memoize the callback */

beats.text: The `callback` parameter type is narrowed from `Event` to `Event & { target: T }`, matching how the body already casts it.
beats.heading: What we change

steps.title: Type signature updated to expose event target
steps.headline: Callback type updated to allow reading the click target
steps.narration: The new container check in the menu's outside-click callback needs to read which element was clicked. The hook's callback type previously did not expose the click target with a usable type, so callers could not access it directly. The signature is narrowed to include the target, matching how the hook body already treats it internally.

summary.problem: The sidebar's z-index was below the top-right UI layer, so UI buttons rendered on top of the open sidebar. A pure z-index raise would then put the sidebar above the main menu on mobile, covering it when both are open at the same time.
summary.solution: Raise the sidebar's z-index above the top-layer UI, and close the floating sidebar whenever the main menu opens. The outside-click guard on the menu trigger is refactored from a data attribute on the button to a DOM container check, which is needed to make the sidebar's outside-click handler correctly close it when the main menu trigger is clicked.

openQuestions.why: Both the inner Island and the outer wrapper div now carry `.dropdown-menu-container`. CSS rules scoped to that class may apply to both levels.
openQuestions.short: Does reusing that class name on the outer wrapper cause style collisions?
openQuestions.question: The class name `.dropdown-menu-container` was already used inside `DropdownMenuContent` for the Island/Stack wrapper. Does the new outer wrapper div using the same class name cause any unintended CSS collisions?

openQuestions.why: `DropdownMenuTrigger` and `DropdownMenu` are generic components reused in multiple places; the attribute removal and the container check affect all of them.
openQuestions.short: Does the attribute removal break other dropdown instances in the app?
openQuestions.question: Any `DropdownMenu` used elsewhere in the app (not just the main menu) now also wraps its trigger in `.dropdown-menu-container`. Does removing `data-prevent-outside-click` from every trigger break the toggle behaviour for any of those other dropdown instances?

openQuestions.why: The `Sidebar.tsx` outside-click handler has `if (!docked || !editorInterface.canFitSidebar)` so it does nothing when docked. On a wide desktop with enough room, a docked sidebar won't close.
openQuestions.short: Does a docked sidebar on desktop stay open when the menu opens?
openQuestions.question: The sidebar only closes when it is floating (not docked). On mobile the sidebar is never docked, so that path is fine — but is there a case where a floating sidebar on desktop could be left open when the main menu opens?
